name: New Partisans
summary: The New Partisans (Serbo-Croatian: Novi Partizani / Нови Партизани) were a short-lived music and visual movement on the Yugoslav rock scene during the mid-1980s.
description:
The New Partisans (Serbo-Croatian: Novi Partizani / Нови Партизани) were a short-lived music and visual movement on the Yugoslav rock scene during the mid-1980s. Centered in Sarajevo, the movement was led by the established band Bijelo Dugme and younger acts Plavi Orkestar and Merlin. [ 1 ]

The aesthetic is defined by a blend of mainstream pop rock with Balkan folk music, but its most distinctive feature was its heavy use of lyrics and imagery inspired by the Yugoslav Partisans of World War II and the state ideology of "Brotherhood and Unity." At a time of rising ethnic nationalism in post-Tito Yugoslavia, the New Partisans movement was a deliberately pro-Yugoslav, anti-nationalist cultural statement. [ 2 ]
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Pro-Yugoslavism, anti-nationalism, nostalgia, brotherhood and unity, pacifism

visualDNA.colour: Muted military tones (olive green, grey), with the prominent use of red

fashion.Overview: A photograph of the band Plavi Orkestar. The members utilize stylized military tunics with decorative gold epaulettes, aiguillettes, and a red star backdrop, illustrating the movement's fusion of Yugoslav socialist iconography with pop stardom. The movement's fashion moved away from standard 1980s rock attire toward a militarized, folk-influenced silhouette. Performers utilized modified World War II-era uniforms and surplus army gear as primary stage garments. Key components of the wardrobe included heavy-duty military boots and partizanke; traditional hand-knitted wool socks historically associated with the Yugoslav Partisans.
